claim: Paper-like small displays support routine electronic reading.
originalWording: Paper-like small displays support routine electronic reading.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 16, printed p. 24

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Small book-sized displays provide high contrast, readable resolution, broad viewing angles and no distracting flicker; digital reading is routine.
reference.rationale: Kindle’s 2007 electronic-paper display and wireless book delivery materially meet the listed visual and reading functions. The forecast did not require all books to abandon print or the screen to share every physical property of paper.

evidence.title: Introducing Amazon Kindle
evidence.note: Reads Like Paper section; Books, Blogs, Magazines and Newspapers section. Amazon describes a reflective electronic-paper screen and wireless access to books and periodicals in 2007. Evidence limits: The display description is a manufacturer claim, not an independent equivalence test against paper.
